A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SIFT research, with matching title and authors. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-L support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Pile language-modeling experiments comparing SIFT with alternative selection methods, alongside ablations and adaptive fine-tuning results in Sections 5-6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including the numerical comparisons in Tables 1-2, extended results, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The SIFT selection rule, surrogate uncertainty model, fine-tuning procedure, adaptive stopping criterion, and efficient implementations in Appendix H are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 17-subdataset Pile coverage for language modeling and retain the same evaluation scenarios and qualitative examples. No datasets or tasks are added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Nearest Neighbor, its repeated-neighbor failure mode, Uncertainty Sampling, in-context learning, and the same model comparators. Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the appendices.

E3.justification: Sections 5-6 and Appendix I retain the same splits, sample sizes, model configurations, preprocessing, fine-tuning budgets, hyperparameters, and bits-per-byte evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The regularization, dataset-size, embedding-normalization, learning-rate, LoRA, and linear-head analyses are retained unchanged, as are the uncertainty analyses and Appendix L qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 90% bootstrap confidence intervals using 1,000 samples and retain the same table-specific standard-error reporting. No repeated-run, seed, or statistical estimation information changes.

E6.justification: All matched scientific tables and plots retain their results. For example, Table 2 reports SIFT fine-tuning results of 0.595 bits per byte for Phi-3 and 0.557 for Llama-3.2 (3B) in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, surrogate-model assumptions, confidence bounds, convergence results, derivations, and appendix proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about SIFT, uncertainty reduction, comparative performance, and adaptive compute. The new Contributions section identifies author roles rather than new scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Explanations of redundancy, relevance versus diversity, uncertainty-based stopping, applicability, and future research remain unchanged, including the extended interpretations in Appendices D-E.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameter tables, hardware information, and code/data links are unchanged. The added author-role statement mentions code optimization but documents no specific technical revision.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Snell et al. is updated from a 2024 arXiv preprint to its ICLR 2025 publication, with the corresponding citation year updated; this is bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v3 adds short Contributions and Acknowledgements sections before References, covering author roles, feedback, and funding. Publication-status text and one reference are updated; the scientific narrative and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Running headers change from preprint status to ICLR 2025 publication status. The new prose reflows the reference pages and shifts appendix pagination, while scientific figures, tables, captions, and their arrangements remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful author-credit and funding disclosures and updates publication metadata. The scientific exposition, evidence, theory, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so these administrative additions do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
